## Why

Once a stay's tier is set, it should stay as it is until the user asks to change it. Today the app revisits it when the stay's nights change. Example: Moab is picked at mid-range as a 3-night stay, under the rule "mid-range for stays of 2+ nights". The user cuts Moab to 1 night. A check note then says "Moab's nights changed from 3 to 1. Its tier was set for 3," and the coordinator asks whether to keep the hotel or see value options (technical spec section 9).

That's inconsistent with how rules work. Nothing revisits a meal's tier or a stay's tier when the user changes a budget rule or the default tier. Joe decided on 2026-10-26, in chat, that both work the same way: a change to the rules or to a stay's nights applies only to tiers set after it. Nothing already set is revisited. The user sees each tier in the itinerary view, and asks for a change if they want one.

So the note, and the code that exists only to raise it, go. That's less deterministic code, and one less rule for the coordinator to follow.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 9 (the paragraph "A stay's tier records the nights it was set for"), and the check table in section 8 (the row "Stay tier set for different nights").
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md): the stay's `tierSetForNightCount` property, its "Tier and nights" paragraph, `setTier()`, and the `stayTierSetForDifferentNights` check kind and its row in the check results table.
- [Research doc: making a whole itinerary read smaller](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/itinerary-read-size.md) (`research/itinerary-read-size.md`), section 5: the whole read proposed for #129 already leaves out the tier's rule and the nights it was set for.

## Open questions

- ~~Saved trips hold `tierSetForNightCount` in each stay of their plan document, and the plan schema is strict (`staySchema` in `src/persistence/itinerary-plan.schema.ts`). So once the field is removed, a saved trip would fail to load. How should saved trips be handled: a one-off update of the saved rows, or a schema that still accepts the key and drops it?~~ Settled 2026-10-26 in PR #149: a one-off update, migration 0008, which also removes saved results of the removed check.

## Do

- Remove the `stayTierSetForDifferentNights` check and its note, and `tierSetForNightCount` on the stay, from the code and its tests. The code is in `src/domain/check-kind.ts`, `check-result.ts`, `stay-checks.ts`, `stay.ts`, `src/persistence/itinerary-document.ts`, `itinerary-plan.schema.ts`, and `src/tools/day-lines.ts`, which writes "set when the stay had N nights" on the "Lodging tier:" line.
- Handle saved trips, as settled in the open question.
- In technical spec section 9, replace the paragraph on nights with the rule above: a change to the rules or to a stay's nights applies only to tiers set after it, and nothing already set is revisited. Remove the check table row in section 8.
- Remove the same parts from the domain model.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, in case a tool description or the coordinator's view file names the note.

## Done when

- The note, the check, and `tierSetForNightCount` are gone from the code, the tests, and the design docs.
- Technical spec section 9 states the rule.
- A saved trip from before the change still loads.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
